title: ClientSurface
description:
Anchor type for the client surface's schema document.

Every wire type on the surface is reachable from here, so a single
`schema_for!` call produces one document with the full type graph in
`$defs`. The struct itself never crosses the wire — it exists only so
the schema generator has a root to walk from.

ApprovalDecisionScope.description: How widely an approved decision should apply.

ChannelLinkCodeResponse.description: A short-lived, single-use channel link code.

ClientEvent.description: Events sent by the client over the WebSocket connection.

oneOf.description: Send a message to the conversation, triggering a provider turn.

Human responds to a pending approval request.

The client sends this event when the user approves or rejects an action
that was held for review by the agent's approval gate. The server
resolves the pending `ApprovalRequired` event and unblocks (or cancels)
the agent turn accordingly.

approval_id.description: Identifies the approval request being resolved.

reason.description: Optional explanation from the human reviewer.

scope.description: How widely an approved decision should apply.

oneOf.description: Cancel the currently active turn.

Subscribe to one or more observability channels by name.

Valid channel names: `"context"`, `"tools"`. Unknown names are silently
ignored so forward-compatible clients do not break on older servers.
Unsubscribe from one or more observability channels by name.
Client requests activating a named skill for the current session.
Client requests deactivating a named skill for the current session.

CreateChannelLinkCodeRequest.description: Request a short-lived code that links a channel conversation to a space.

CreateConversationRequest.description:
Request body for the conversation and space-session creation endpoints.

Every field is optional and the body itself may be omitted: an absent
`agent_id` selects the default `"gateway"` agent, and an absent
`selected_model_id` leaves the session's model unselected. A named
`agent_id` must be `"gateway"` or an agent definition visible to the
target space; the gateway rejects anything else with a validation error.

message.description: What each run asks the agent to do.

routing.description: Defaults to local-record-only routing when omitted.

delivery_grant.description:
Server-side delivery targets granted to this script. Responses expose
only whether a grant exists, never its URLs or secret references.

DeliveryRoutingRequest.description:
Where output should be routed once a run completes.

`deliver_to_origin` defaults to true for channel-initiated turns, where
an origin always exists. Callers without an origin (schedules, manual
API calls) must set it false or target resolution errors.

DeliveryTarget.description: A destination for a run's output.

ExternalChannelIntegration.description: An external channel integration that can receive delivered output.

GateConfig.description:
A cheap-model check that runs before the main model wakes.

The gate model inspects the schedule's message, the optional criteria,
and the previous run's outcome, then verdicts `run` or `skip`. Its
decision and reasoning are recorded on the run.

criteria.description:
What "work needed" means for this schedule. When absent the gate
judges from the schedule message and previous outcome alone.

model.description: Model id or alias from the configured model catalogue.

GateDecision.description: A gate decision as recorded on a run.

offset.description: Byte offset of `passage` when it can be located in the derivation.

Schedule.description: A schedule as returned by the API.

creator.description: Where this schedule came from — a person or an agent.

ScheduleCreator.description:
Who created a schedule.

This is provenance, not a request field: the surface that creates the
schedule stamps it (the settings UI and HTTP surface stamp `user`; the
scheduling tools stamp `agent`), so an agent cannot claim a schedule was
a person's. It answers the audit question "where did this schedule come
from" wherever schedules are listed.

oneOf.description: A person, through the settings automation panel or the HTTP surface.

An agent, through the scheduling tools. Carries the id of the agent
that made it.

ScheduleGateUpdate.description:
How an update touches a schedule's gate.

A gate is an optional field, and clearing an optional field over the
wire needs a value distinct from "leave unchanged". So the gate slot on
an update is itself optional: absent leaves the gate as it stands, while
a present value is one of these two actions.

oneOf.description: Install this gate, replacing any existing one.
Remove the gate entirely.

ScheduleRun.description: A recorded run: everything needed to reconstruct what happened.

session_id.description:
The session the run executed in — created fresh or continued,
depending on the schedule's session policy. Absent when the run
never reached a session (gated out, or skipped for overlap).

ScheduleRunState.description: Lifecycle state of a recorded run.

oneOf.description: Completed successfully but produced no assistant text.
Deliberately not executed — see the run's `skip_reason`.

ScheduleRunTrigger.description: What caused a run to be created.

oneOf.description: The scheduler's clock reached the schedule's next occurrence.
An operator fired the schedule by hand.

ScheduleSpec.description:
When a schedule fires.

- `one_shot` — a single RFC 3339 instant.
- `interval` — natural-language `"every N seconds|minutes|hours|days"`.
- `cron` — a cron expression (seconds-resolution, as parsed by the
  `cron` crate).

ScheduleStatus.description: Lifecycle status of a schedule definition.

oneOf.description:
A one-shot that has fired, or an interval/cron with no next
occurrence.

SchemaValidationError.description: A single JSON Schema validation error from output schema checking.

message.description: Human-readable description of the constraint that was violated.

path.description: JSON pointer to the failing location (e.g. `"/properties/name"`).

ServerEvent.description: Events sent by the server to the client over the WebSocket connection.

oneOf.description: A token streamed from the provider.
A tool call has begun execution. Correlates with a later ToolEnd via call_id.

parent_call_id.description:
call_id of the enclosing tool if this is a sub-tool invocation.

Omitted from the serialised JSON when None so existing clients that
do not handle sub-tools remain unaffected.

oneOf.description: A tool call has finished. Contains the result and execution metadata.

parent_call_id.description:
call_id of the enclosing tool if this is a sub-tool invocation.

Omitted from the serialised JSON when None.

oneOf.description:
Context assembly completed for a turn.

Contains the full assembly report for diagnostics and token budget
inspection. Only delivered to connections subscribed to the `"context"`
channel unless the report contains errors, in which case it is always
sent so the client can surface assembly failures to the user.

The report is carried as `serde_json::Value` to decouple the wire
format from swage-context's internal types — the shape matches
`swage_context::report::AssemblyReport` when serialised.

The provider has finished and the turn has been committed.

The base event always includes `turn_id`. Usage fields are populated
only for connections subscribed to the `"context"` channel — unsubscribed
clients receive `turn_id` alone (the `skip_serializing_if` annotation
keeps the JSON shape backward-compatible).

structured_output.description:
Validated, parsed JSON output when an output schema was configured and
validation passed. Absent (serialised as omitted) when no schema is
configured or when validation failed after retry exhaustion.

oneOf.description:
A schema validation attempt failed and the agent will retry.

Only delivered to connections subscribed to the `"context"` channel —
these are observability events that provide retry progress to developers
and diagnostic tooling. Normal clients that have not subscribed do not
receive intermediate retry noise.

max_retries.description: Maximum configured retries for this turn.

oneOf.description: Provider retry progress for the active turn.
Provider retry wait has settled.

All schema validation retries were exhausted without a valid response.

Always delivered regardless of subscription state — this is an error
condition that the client must surface to the user.

attempts.description: Total number of attempts made (including the initial attempt).

errors.description: Validation errors from the final attempt.

oneOf.description:
A delegation from one agent to another has started.
Always delivered — clients need delegation lifecycle events to track
sub-agent progress regardless of subscription state.

A delegation has completed (successfully or with failure).
Always delivered — matches DelegationStarted semantics.
A detached workflow run has started.
A workflow journal entry changed state.
A detached workflow run reached a terminal state.
An error occurred during or before turn processing.
A pending turn was successfully cancelled.

The server is shutting down. Clients should clean up and disconnect.

Always delivered regardless of subscription state — a client that
misses this event will simply see the connection close without a
graceful handshake.

A skill was successfully activated for the current session.

Includes metadata so the client can display the skill without a
separate lookup.

token_count.description: Token budget consumed by this skill's instructions in the context window.

oneOf.description: A skill was already active — no state change occurred.
A skill was successfully deactivated for the current session.

A tool call (or other action) requires human approval before proceeding.

Delivered when the agent's dispatch pipeline raises an approval gate.
The client should present the approval UI and respond with a
`ClientEvent::ApprovalDecision` before `timeout_at` elapses.

approval_id.description: Unique identifier for this approval request.

context.description: Additional context the client may render to assist the decision.

kind.description: Category of the action requiring approval (e.g. `"tool_call"`).

prompt.description: Human-readable description of the action to be approved.

timeout_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp after which the approval is considered expired.

tool_arguments.description: Parsed arguments of the tool call, for display in the approval UI.

tool_name.description: Name of the tool involved, if the approval is for a tool call.

turn_id.description: Turn that triggered the approval gate.

oneOf.description:
The approval decision has been recorded and forwarded to the agent.

Sent to the client that submitted the decision as an acknowledgement,
and broadcast to other clients on the same session for consistency.

approval_id.description: Identifier of the resolved approval request.

reason.description: Optional explanation provided by the human reviewer.

oneOf.description:
An approval request timed out before a decision was submitted.

The `timeout_policy` field indicates the action that was taken
automatically as a result of the expiry.

approval_id.description: Identifier of the expired approval request.

oneOf.description:
A submitted approval decision was rejected by the server.

Possible causes include attempting to decide an already-resolved request
or submitting an unknown `approval_id`. The `error` field carries a
machine-readable code; `message` gives a human-readable explanation.

approval_id.description: Identifier of the approval request that could not be decided.

current_state.description: Current state of the request, if known (e.g. `"approved"`, `"expired"`).

oneOf.description:
A gateway event this client version does not understand.

This is constructed by the Rust client after a tagged event fails to
deserialise; the gateway never emits it directly.

SessionPolicy.description:
Which session each run executes in.

- `fresh` — every run creates a new session in `space_id` for
  `agent_id`, with a deliberately assembled opening context (the
  schedule's message plus the previous run's outcome).
- `continuation` — every run continues the named session, executing as
  whatever agent that session has at run time.

SkipReason.description: Why a run was skipped rather than executed.

oneOf.description: The gate model decided no work was needed.

A previous run of this schedule (or another turn in the target
session) was still executing when this run came due.

UpdateScheduleRequest.description:
Partially update a schedule.

The session policy is fixed at creation — delete and recreate to change
where runs execute.

gate.description: Set or clear the gate. Absent leaves the existing gate untouched.

reserved_closing_tokens.description:
Tokens held back from ordinary work for calls made after the run has
observed its wind-down boundary. This allowance is part of, not in
addition to, `max_total_tokens`.

oneOf.description:
A pending-queue operation: an event posted, or events stamped
delivered by a wake.

A wake-gate evaluation: a cheap model judged the pending events; its
verdict and reasoning are the entry's result.

A journalled budget reading — what the script saw when it checked
its allowance, replayed rather than re-read.

The working allowance was exhausted. The triggering agent call was
not started; replay returns the same wind-down signal at this point.

wake_metrics.description:
The run's own wake economics, derived from the journal and event
queue — the falsification signal for a gated long run: a sustained
high wake rate means the design's economics are failing.

oneOf.description:
Sleeping on a durable wait with its engine torn down; the waker
resumes it by journal replay when it is due.

WorkflowWakeMetrics.description:
Derived counters over a run's wake machinery. `events_pending` counts
undelivered queue entries now; the rest count journalled history.
